survivors.claim: --cite accepts a path that prefix-matches the spec shape but resolves via '..' to a non-spec file, so a raise can be recorded citing something that is not a spec. CITE_RE is only start-anchored and the existence check runs path.join (which normalizes '..') before existsSync. The spec's own D4 regex (^specs/\d{8}/\d{2}-) is equally start-only, so this is not a contradiction of the spec text - hygiene only; the live AC-9 pin would also pass such a cite.
survivors.impact: A raise can be logged with a citation that points at something other than a spec, so the trace from growth back to the feature that asked for it can be faked by a malformed path.
survivors.evidence: Synthetic tmpdir git repo, seeded baseline: '--raise tests/a.txt --to 20 --cite specs/20260909/01-x.md/../../../size-baseline.json' -> exit=0, raises [{path:'tests/a.txt',from:10,to:20,cite:'specs/20260909/01-x.md/../../../size-baseline.json'}]. Code: line 355 CITE_RE.test(args.cite) with CITE_RE = /^specs\/\d{8}\/\d{2}-/ (no end anchor), 358-359 path.join(root, args.cite) then existsSync.

survivors.claim: The header's exit-2 list (lines 25-28) enumerates the raise/cite/target triggers but omits three exit-2 paths the script implements: a non-integer --to (line 353), --json combined with --update/--raise (line 77), and --update together with --raise (line 76). Same exit code, so not the hard undocumented-exit-code class - the same shape the prior round graded soft for the exit-1 line.
survivors.impact: A reader relying on the header to learn why an invocation was rejected is told most but not all of the reasons.
survivors.evidence: '--raise tests/a.txt --to 12.5 --cite specs/20260909/01-x.md' -> exit=2 '--to must be a non-negative integer byte count, got 12.5'; adding --json -> exit=2 '--json is not compatible with --update or --raise'; '--update --raise ...' -> exit=2 '--update and --raise are mutually exclusive'.
